10                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

11   Resolution Number 1459, by Senator Hoylman, 

12   memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

13   proclaim April 24, 2015, as World Meningitis Day 

14   in the State of New York.

15                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

16   Hoylman.

17                SENATOR HOYLMAN:   Thank you, 

18   Mr. President.  

19                I just wanted to take a few minutes 

20   to speak about this resolution which proclaims 

21   April 24th, tomorrow, as World Meningitis Day in 

22   the State of New York.

23                The resolution is really designed 

24   to increase awareness of the deadliness of 

25   bacterial meningitis and the importance of 


                                                                2069

 1   preemptive immunization campaigns in preventing 

 2   outbreaks of meningitis here in New York and 

 3   across the country.

 4                You know, 25 percent of us carry the 

 5   meningitis strain in our nose or our mouth.  So 

 6   that's 15.75 Senators who are carriers.  We might 

 7   not get sick from it, but we are infectious to 

 8   other people.  And if other people are in fact 

 9   infected with meningitis, it can cause severe 

10   brain damage and it's fatal in about 50 percent 

11   of the cases.  

12                It's especially frightening because 

13   it occurs so swiftly.  Some victims are found 

14   dead in their beds before they've even had a 

15   chance to seek medical attention.  And the 

16   initial symptoms are very innocuous.  It could be 

17   just a stiff neck or a headache, but it rapidly, 

18   rapidly progresses.

19                Now, the issue carries particular 

20   weight in my district because it was the 

21   epicenter of an unnerving outbreak in 2012 that 

22   has lasted for several years, and it's had a 

23   particular impact on the LGBT population.  

24   Although we often associate meningitis with 

25   college dorms and military barracks, gay men are 


                                                                2070

 1   often the victims too.  

 2                And the outbreak was only contained 

 3   and kept at bay due to the tireless work of a 

 4   number of City Health Department officials, 

 5   including Dr. Demetre Daskalakis and Dr. Jay 

 6   Varma.  Dr. Daskalakis went into nightclubs and 

 7   private parties and inoculated young gay men with 

 8   the meningitis vaccination one by one.  And 

 9   thousands of men across the city were 

10   inoculated, and it staved off an outbreak that 

11   could have been much worse.  And this direct 

12   community-based approach was very successful.  

13                We here, though, in the Senate did 

14   something too, and I wanted to thank my 

15   colleagues Senator Ken LaValle and Senator Kemp 

16   Hannon for working with me on passing a bill in 

17   2013 to allow licensed pharmacists and certified 

18   nurse practitioners to administer the meningitis 

19   vaccination to adults 18 years or older.  And 

20   this is an important safeguard as well.

21                We're very fortunate to have public 

22   health officials and colleagues in this body who 

23   recognize the importance of getting inoculated.  

24   Whether you're a preteen, age 16 to 21, a kid age 

25   11 to 12, college students, military recruits, 


                                                                2071

 1   people who are HIV-positive or gay men, you 

 2   should strongly consider the advice of the CDC 

 3   and get inoculated even tomorrow on World 

 4   Meningitis Day.  

 5                Thank you, Mr. President.
